messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — ran a small profiling pass against the 13B kernel candidates on staging this morning. Found an unexpected tail latency bump for sequence lengths >1024 when the new fused-attn kernel is selected. Attached a quick token-level heatmap in the dashboard.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the top-level numbers? Is this across all routes or only long-context routes? :thinking_face:

Alex Chen: Short summary:
- per-token p50/p95 unaffected
- p99 increased ~18% for seq>1024
- tail shows up only on routes where batching heuristic allows larger batch_size at warm cache (not when cache cold)

Linh Tran: Interesting — that suggests kernel/caching interaction. Did you capture KV cache hit rate during the runs?

Alex Chen: Yes. When cache hit rate >85% and average prefix length >512 we see the bump. When KV hit <50% the bump disappears (regression seems tied to prefix reuse + fused-attn path).

Tess Morgan: That smells like the fused kernel's memory access pattern making KV lookup+merge slower at high reuse. Any profiler traces? Can we see a flamegraph?

Alex Chen: Pulled a perf trace and lightweight flame graph:

```
# condensed stack samples
fused_attn_kernel
  -> kv_merge_batch
    -> memcpy
    -> cuda_memset
    -> kernel_dispatch
```

We see increased memcpy time proportional to sequence length.

Priya Rao: From an alerting POV, this only impacts a subset of customers/routes. We should add a per-route token-latency breakdown panel and a burn-rate alarm on p99-token-latency for routes serving long-context workloads. Current SLOs are global and mask this.

Linh Tran: Agree. Suggested thresholds:
- route-level p99-token-latency > 250ms for 5m -> page
- burn-rate alarm if consumed-error-budget >2x for 10m

Tess Morgan: Also add a detector for sudden correlation between KV hit rate and p99 increase. Anomaly rule: if correlation coefficient >0.6 over last 15m, create a ticket.

perf-bot: deploy finished for canary group 'fused-attn-v2' at 2025-12-05T09:40:28Z :white_check_mark:

Alex Chen: Reproduced locally by forcing fused-attn path + prefilled KV cache. Short-term mitigation: pin the kernel to reference-attn for routes with avg_prefix >600 until we root cause. Will open rollout-blocker PR.

Priya Rao: OK — add dashboard widgets:
- per-route token p50/p95/p99 heatmap
- KV hit-rate overlay
- kernel selection ratio (fused vs reference)

Also add an alert that triggers when the kernel-selection-ratio for any route changes >30% within 10m (to catch accidental rollouts).

Linh Tran: For the rollout PR, can we add an automatic fallback in router: if p99_token_latency increases >20% after 2m of deploy, auto-switch to fallback kernel? That would prevent pages.

Tess Morgan: Good idea. We'll need safety limits to avoid flip-flopping. Add a cool-down of 15m and max 1 auto-fallback per hour per route.

Alex Chen: I'll draft the PR and update the dashboard in Grafana. Putting notes in the PR: repro steps, perf trace, mitigation, suggested alert thresholds, and canary criteria.

Priya Rao: Thanks — please ping #oncall if you flip the kernel in prod. Also ping me before changing SLO definitions.

Alex Chen: Will do. TL;DR: kernel selection + KV cache interaction caused p99 token tail on long contexts; dashboards + route alerts + temporary kernel pin + auto-fallback are the plan.

Tess Morgan: :thumbsup:
